metadata.title: The Reallocation Engine
metadata.purpose: Explain what the Reallocation Engine is, what evidence it weighs, what it recommends, and where the human decision stays.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sanjana Alapati, and this video is about the Reallocation Engine and how it helps OPT students focus their job search.
beats.new_visual_element: The ask, typed into the Claude composer

props.command: I'm on OPT with a limited unemployment clock. Help me decide which roles are actually worth applying to — and which to skip.
output: sponsorship history · posting liveness · role quality
Apply · Consider · Skip — every source labeled

beats.narration_text: Applying to more jobs does not always mean making more progress. For students on OPT, unemployment time is limited, so it becomes important to focus on opportunities that are actually worth pursuing.
beats.new_visual_element: The arriving assumption, typed — then corrected on screen

props.text:
More applications means more progress.
On OPT the clock is the scarce resource —
not the effort.

beats.narration_text: The Reallocation Engine is designed for international students on F-1 OPT who are searching for jobs after graduation and need a more focused way to evaluate opportunities.
beats.new_visual_element: Who the engine is for — three plain lines

beats.narration_text: Instead of relying only on guesswork, the engine looks at several signals, including sponsorship history, whether the job is still active, role quality, resume fit, and whether the opportunity works with the student's OPT timeline.
beats.new_visual_element: Five evidence chips, arriving one per named signal

beats.narration_text: These signals are combined into an overall recommendation. Some factors can matter more than others, and issues like an inactive job posting or a timeline that does not work can outweigh otherwise positive signals.
beats.new_visual_element: Signals combine into one recommendation; the deal-breakers are struck out

props.note: Some signals carry more weight than others.
props.banned: Inactive posting, or a timeline that cannot work

beats.narration_text: Based on the available evidence, an opportunity can be grouped into Apply, Consider, or Skip, helping students focus their effort where it matters most.
beats.new_visual_element: The recommendation as an artifact — three grouped outcomes

artifactLines: Apply — the evidence supports spending real time here.
Consider — worth a look, with something still unresolved.
Skip — the evidence says this effort is better spent elsewhere.

beats.narration_text: But the Reallocation Engine does not replace human judgment. Public data cannot capture every detail or recent change, so the recommendation is meant to support the student, while the final decision remains theirs.
beats.new_visual_element: The limit stated plainly — what public data cannot see

meta: Where it fails: a role that changed last week still reads as last month's record.

beats.narration_text: My main takeaway is simple: use the evidence to focus your effort, but keep the final decision in your hands. Use the evidence. Trust your judgment.

lines: Use the evidence to focus your effort.
Keep the final decision in your hands.
Use the evidence. Trust your judgment.
